To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the production of glueballs and hybrid states in quark and in gluon jets is a sensitive probe for the colour confinement process in the final state; b) the production of light JPC=0+ glueballs in quark jets is enhanced compared to gluon jets, if colour octet neutralisation dominates; c) the production of hybrids in gluon jets may be enhanced compared to quark jets, independent of the neutralisation process.
the fragmentation of gluons into glueballs and hybrids is a very interesting process that can be used to study the confinement properties of the QCD vacuum.
